source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 11 mathematics textbooks (advanced stream)

stages.headline: A ⇒ B («if A then B») is false only when A is true and B is false; A ⇔ B is true when A and B have the same value.
stages.headlineEnglish: A ⇒ B («if A then B») is false only when A is true and B is false; A ⇔ B is true when A and B have the same value.

stages.headline: x = 2 ⇒ x² = 4 is true, but x² = 4 ⇒ x = 2 is not (x = −2); a true equivalence is x² = 4 ⇔ x = ±2.
stages.headlineEnglish: x = 2 ⇒ x² = 4 is true, but x² = 4 ⇒ x = 2 is not (x = −2); a true equivalence is x² = 4 ⇔ x = ±2.

stages.headline: In A ⇒ B, A is a sufficient condition for B and B a necessary condition for A: «ends in 0» ⇒ «is even».
stages.headlineEnglish: In A ⇒ B, A is a sufficient condition for B and B a necessary condition for A: «ends in 0» ⇒ «is even».

stages.headline: A is true, B is false. What is A ⇒ B?

stages.headline: Is «x² > 9 ⇔ x > 3» true?
stages.solutionSteps: 1. x = −4 gives x² > 9 but not x > 3.
stages.solutionStepsEnglish: 1. x = −4 gives x² > 9 but not x > 3.
